# FDG3023

> DO NOT use the “Ex” (or a similar) suffix for an identifier to distinguish it from an earlier version of the same API.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.2.4 Naming New Versions of Existing APIs.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1711
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1711 reports the Ex and New suffixes when a member or type without the suffix exists. Unlike the other versioning guidelines it applies to applications too, as a naming rule (CA1711 is shared with FDG3052, FDG3055, FDG3062, and FDG3063). Removing the suffix renames a public member or type, which changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1711 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
[Obsolete("This type is obsolete. ...")]
public class Car  { ... }

// new API
public class CarEx      { ... } // the wrong way
public class CarNew     { ... } // the wrong way
public class Car2       { ... } // an acceptable way
public class Automobile { ... } // a better way
```
